description:
Summary: develop a live perception stack for the Amica satellite install that turns camera and microphone streams into structured real-time signals usable by the UI, automation, and future hub/gateway behaviors. Scope: define and implement three coordinated modules under this epic: (1) human action recognition on live camera video with structured Body/Hand/Head outputs, (2) facial emotion recognition on live camera video with current facial emotion output, and (3) live microphone separation plus real-time speaker identity/voiceprint output. Requirements: keep modules suitable for Pi-local deployment where feasible, expose machine-readable outputs with stable schemas, and preserve a clear path for telemetry to flow into Amica/hub/gateway consumers. Validation: each child module has a documented runtime contract, live-input integration path, and targeted verification on real device streams.

description:
Summary: develop a live audio module that consumes microphone input, separates concurrent or overlapping speakers where feasible, and emits real-time speaker identity telemetry. Scope: build voiceprint-based speaker identification suitable for ongoing conversation on the satellite path, with explicit handling for unknown speakers and changing confidence. Output contract: expose machine-readable state/events for active speaker identity, confidence, timing, and separation metadata so hub/gateway/Amica consumers can attribute speech correctly. Expectations: operate on live microphone input with minimal added latency, preserve a clear mute/unmute boundary, and document any Pi-local versus offloaded compute split. Validation: live microphone test demonstrates stable speaker identity output, unknown-speaker behavior, and documented schema/transport.

description:
Summary: develop a facial emotion recognition module that consumes the live camera stream and outputs the subject's current facial emotion in real time. Scope: detect the primary face, classify current emotion, and expose a machine-readable state that includes timestamp, confidence, and current label. Expectations: integrate with the existing live video path, handle no-face and low-confidence states explicitly, and keep the output stable enough for Amica-side behavior or UI use. Validation: live camera test shows real-time emotion updates with a documented schema, confidence behavior, and no-face handling.

description:
Summary: develop a human action recognition module that consumes the live camera stream and emits structured real-time action telemetry. Scope: detect and classify observable actions across three dimensions: Body, Hand, and Head. Output contract: provide machine-readable events/state with stable fields for timestamp, confidence, and per-dimension labels so downstream Amica/hub consumers can react without image parsing. Expectations: support continuous inference on live video, handle loss/reacquisition cleanly, and keep the runtime viable for Pi-local execution or an explicitly defined offload path if needed. Example outputs: body posture or gross movement state, hand gesture/action state, and head orientation/action state. Validation: live camera test demonstrates low-latency structured output for all three dimensions and documents the schema and transport path.
